content:
sara.support: Heads-up: we've got a customer ticket — private VPC endpoint for acme-infra reporting intermittent 502s. Monitoring shows an intermediate cert in their uploaded bundle expiring in ~72 hours. @acme-infra can you confirm if you have a rotation plan?

acme-infra: We saw the 502 spike around 02:10 UTC this morning, yes. Restarting the proxy didn't help. We haven't rotated the uploaded bundle since last month.

cert-rotator-bot: automated-check: customer-uploaded-bundle check → warning: intermediate cert expires 2026-03-20 04:33:12 UTC; chain length=2 (missing intermediate? recommended fullchain length=3).

sara.support: Thanks. Can you paste the client-side error you see and the output of an openssl connect test? Quick repro helps us confirm whether the server is serving an incomplete chain.

acme-infra: Curl error from our healthchecks: `curl: (60) SSL certificate: unable to get local issuer certificate`
OpenSSL snippet: ```
$ openssl s_client -showcerts -connect private-api.acme.internal:443 -servername private-api.acme.internal
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = private-api.acme.internal
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
Certificate chain
0 s:/CN=private-api.acme.internal
  i:/CN=acme-intermediate
---
# no further chain certificates presented by server
```

dan.prodeng: Sounds like the server is not sending the intermediate. If the client only has the root in its truststore, the handshake fails. Two common causes: (1) uploaded bundle missing the intermediate, or (2) proxy (HAProxy/nginx) truncating chain due to mis-ordered PEMs. Also check if your client is blocked from fetching AIA/OCSP (some clients try to pull intermediate via AIA).

alice.networks: Also confirm egress allowlist — if your VPC blocks outbound to public CAs/OCSP responders, certain validation paths can fail. Which firewall rules do you have for outbound? Any NAT IP changes recently?

acme-infra: Our egress is locked down. Current outbound rules only allow HTTPS to a small set of partner IPs (we whitelist by CIDR). We didn't add any CA/OCSP IPs. Could that cause this?

sara.support: If the cert bundle is missing an intermediate, egress won't help unless clients rely on AIA fetching (which not all do). Rotator does NOT auto-fetch missing intermediates for customer-uploaded bundles — we expect a fullchain PEM. Immediate options: (A) reupload fullchain.pem that includes leaf + intermediate(s) in the correct order, (B) add the missing intermediate to your clients' truststore, or (C) temporarily relax egress to allow OCSP/AIA fetch (not ideal). We'll guide you through (A) since it's quickest.

dan.prodeng: Also collect haproxy/nginx cert file used by the proxy, confirm ordering: leaf first, then intermediate(s), then root (root optional). If using our cert rotator UI, the upload should accept fullchain. If the uploaded file had the intermediate missing or out of order we should warn — I'll follow up to add a warning in the rotator upload path.

sara.support: Repro/check commands for you to run locally before upload: ```
# verify chain file locally
openssl verify -CAfile /etc/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt fullchain.pem
# inspect ordering and certificates
awk 'BEGIN{c=0} /BEGIN CERTIFICATE/{c++; print "--- cert " c} {print} /END CERTIFICATE/{print ""}' fullchain.pem | sed -n '1,120p'
# test server presentation
openssl s_client -showcerts -connect private-api.acme.internal:443 -servername private-api.acme.internal
```
Paste the output if you want us to validate.

acme-infra: OK we're going to reupload the bundle with the intermediate. One question: does the rotator require the root in the bundle?

sara.support: Root is optional in the server-side bundle — include leaf then intermediate(s). Do NOT include extraneous certs. After upload, restart or reload the proxy (HAProxy: `systemctl reload haproxy` or `service haproxy reload`) — that should trigger the new chain to be served.

acme-infra: Reuploaded fullchain (leaf + intermediate), reloaded HAProxy, healthchecks back to green. Errors dropped to baseline. Thanks! :thumbsup:

sara.support: Great. Follow-ups: @dan.prodeng please add a server-side monitor that flags uploaded bundles missing intermediates and an expiry <7d warning in the rotator UI. @alice.networks please add a KB note about egress/OCSP implications for customer truststores. I'll update the support playbook with the repro commands and quick remediation steps. Marking this thread resolved unless anyone needs further help.

dan.prodeng: Acknowledged — filing an internal ticket to add warnings + small UI badge for chain completeness.

alice.networks: Acknowledged, will add a short doc and a checklist for customers with strict egress.

deploy-bot: incident-note: customer fix verified, no further rolling restarts needed.

sara.support: Closing — reopen if issue recurs.
